title: For the 20 leads that assemble a stack per client, the demo binds to whichever tool the client already runs
content:
These leads have no single named tool of their own; the paired fit finding records that they assemble a stack per client. The demo therefore cannot be pre-bound to a product, and the research text does not try: pick one tool from their published stack, have a webhook or hook dispatch a typed operation, then delete the source record and replay it from Powerhouse. The text states the reason the shape survives that indeterminacy — the demo is stack-agnostic because the gap is.

The practical consequence is that tool selection moves from research output to conversation input. For an integrator whose stack is chosen per engagement, asking which system the current client runs is a normal opening question rather than a gap in preparation, and the answer determines the hook without changing anything else about the demonstration.

The cohort is 20 leads, weighted to DE, FR and IT with single entries in BE, CH, ES and AT. None is priority 1: 16 sit at "3 · later" and four are unprioritised. So this is a demo shape that is cheap to reuse against a cold cohort, and its value is that it costs nothing extra rather than that it unlocks anything immediately.
